newsitem.title: UK: British homeless to be helped by toilet advertising.
newsitem.headline: British homeless to be helped by toilet advertising.

text.p: Homeless Britons will benefit from a novel form of advertising -- posters strategically placed at eye level in public toilets.

The Big Issue, a weekly magazine sold on British streets in aid of the homeless, has linked up with advertisers CPA to promote a new CD of electronic music in London's pubs and nightclubs, a CPA statement said.
Posters promoting the CD will be put in toilets for an "exciting, funny and vibrant" form of advertising. Toilet doors and walls are wasted space at present, CPA said.
"Careful and thorough research has indicated that most people spend between 30 seconds and three minutes at this activity," a CPA statement said.
"With over 700 million toilet visits each year this form of advertising cannot fail to be a success."
All profits from the sale of the CD will be paid directly to the Big Issue which helps the estimated 365,000 homeless in Britain.
